etymologies.etymologyHTML:
Originally British English; as an abbreviation for association football, via abbreviation assoc. +‎ -er (suffix); earlier socker (1885), also socca (1889), with soccer attested 1888.

Compare contemporary rugger, from Rugby. Similarly constructed coinages from the same period include: brekker (“breakfast”), fresher (“freshman”) and footer (“football”). See Oxford -er.

definitions.definition: (originated, late 19th C, now often US, Australia, Ireland, Philippines, and other countries; see usage notes) Association football.

quote.citation: 1885 December, “Our Oxford Letter”, in The Oldhallian‎[1], page 171:
quote.text: The 'Varsity played Aston Villa and were beaten after a very exciting game; this was pre-eminently the most important "Socker" game played in Oxford this term.

quote.citation: 1888 February 15, “Charley Symonds”, in The Oxford Magazine‎[2], page 224:
quote.text: Golf is perhaps seven or eight years old in Oxford, ... football, seu Rugger, sive Soccer, not more than sixteen or seventeen.

quote.citation: 1889 September 16, “Football Prospects in the West of England”, in The Western Daily Press, volume 63, number 9757, Bristol, page 7:
quote.text: Those who play under the "Socker" (Association) rules in the North of England, the Midlands, and Scotland take no heed of the warmness of the weather

quote.citation: 1890, Albert Barrère, Charles Leland, A Dictionary of Slang, Jargon & Cant‎[3], volume 2, Ballantyne, page 275:
quote.text: Socker (public schools), football played according to the Association Rules

definitions.definition: (Australian rules football) To kick the football directly off the ground, without using one's hands.

quote.citation: 1990, Geoffrey Blainey, A Game of Our Own: The Origins of Australian Football, Black Inc. Publishing, published 2003, page 73:
quote.text: The rule seems to have encouraged players to soccer the ball along the ground.

quote.citation: 2008, John Devaney, Full Points Footy′s WA Football Companion, page 334:
quote.text: […] West Perth seemed on the verge of victory, only to succumb by 4 points after a soccered goal from Old Easts with less than half a minute remaining.

quote.citation: 2010 March 27, Michael Whiting, “Lions give Fev debut to remember”, in AFL - The official site of the Australian Football League:
quote.text: Fevola showed the best and worst of his play after dropping a simple chest mark, only to regather seconds later and soccer the ball through from the most acute of angles.
